### 🌲 Computational Ecology, Data Analytics & Remote Sensing

The CEDAR Lab builds computational methods and open-source software for understanding how forests and landscapes change — combining machine learning, satellite remote sensing, and spatial analysis to answer questions that matter for conservation, carbon, and biodiversity.

[The CEDAR Lab on GitHub](https://github.com/thecedarlab){.cta-btn .cta-primary style="margin-top: 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem; padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;"}
[Our research](research.qmd){.cta-btn .cta-secondary style="margin-top: 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem; padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;"}
:::

## What CEDAR stands for

**C**omputational **E**cology, **D**ata **A**nalytics, and **R**emote sensing — the three strands that run through everything the lab does.

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card-item}
[🧮]{.card-icon}

### Computational Ecology
Turning ecological questions into models that can be run, tested, and re-run. Simulation of forest dynamics and disturbance sits alongside statistical inference from field and satellite observation.

[Modeling]{.card-tag} [Simulation]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[📊]{.card-icon}

### Data Analytics
Machine learning and spatial statistics applied to large, messy environmental datasets — with an emphasis on validation that holds up when a model meets a landscape it has never seen.

[Machine Learning]{.card-tag} [Spatial Stats]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[🛰️]{.card-icon}

### Remote Sensing
Openly licensed Earth observation — Landsat, Sentinel, LiDAR, radar — used to measure forest structure, composition, and change from the individual crown to the continental scale.

[Earth Observation]{.card-tag} [LiDAR]{.card-tag}
:::

:::

## How we work

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Open by default

Code, methods, and — where licensing allows — data are released publicly. Software is archived on Zenodo so it carries a citable DOI, and analyses are built as reproducible pipelines rather than one-off scripts that only run on one machine.

### Free and open data

The lab deliberately builds on openly licensed Earth observation and environmental data: Landsat, Sentinel, SoilGrids, LANDFIRE, and ESA WorldCover. Methods that depend on commercial imagery budgets are methods most of the world cannot use.

### Tools, not just papers

Research outputs are packaged so other people can actually run them — QGIS plugins, R packages, documented workflows. A result that stops at a figure in a paper is only half finished.

### Teaching in the open

Methods are explained publicly through written tutorials and the [GeoAI for Ecology](https://www.youtube.com/@geoai4ecology) YouTube channel, so that researchers without a computational background can pick these tools up.

:::

## Software

The lab's software is developed in the open. Everything is free to use, inspect, and build on.

::: {.card-grid .two-col}

::: {.card-item}
[🌲]{.card-icon}

### iLAND Workbench
A QGIS plugin bringing the iLAND individual-based forest landscape and disturbance model into a GIS workflow — runtime management, climate and soil data pipelines, and reproducible analysis. Archived on Zenodo with a citable DOI.

[Documentation](tools.qmd#iland-workbench) · [Source](https://github.com/paudelsushil/iLAND-QGIS-plugin)

[QGIS Plugin]{.card-tag} [Python]{.card-tag} [Released]{.card-tag}
:::

::: {.card-item}
[📦]{.card-icon}

### forestPulse
An R package for analysing forest structure and disturbance from field plots and drone or satellite imagery, and for assembling the climate, landscape, and tree-initialisation inputs that drive the iLand model. Released under MIT with a citable DOI.

[Documentation](tools.qmd#forestpulse) · [Source](https://github.com/paudelsushil/forestPulse)

[R Package]{.card-tag} [R]{.card-tag} [Released]{.card-tag}
:::

:::

## Research themes

The lab's active work spans four connected areas. Each is described in more detail on the [research page](research.qmd).

::: {.card-grid .two-col}

::: {.card-item}
[🛰️]{.card-icon}

### Forest disturbance mapping
Detecting deforestation, degradation, and recovery from satellite time series, separating gradual change from abrupt clearing.
:::

::: {.card-item}
[🌍]{.card-icon}

### Landscape connectivity
Modeling how fragmentation shapes species movement, gene flow, and ecosystem resilience.
:::

::: {.card-item}
[📈]{.card-icon}

### Spatial modeling
Species distribution and biomass models built with spatially aware validation.
:::

::: {.card-item}
[🌿]{.card-icon}

### Biodiversity assessment
Multi-sensor habitat characterization across scales, fusing optical, radar, and LiDAR data.
:::

:::
